Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

poverty noun

also being poor, want, destitution, penury, helplessness

classical

Cic. Par. 45: paupertātem vel potius egestātem ac mendīcitātem (Lewis & Short)
Ov. Met. 8.633: paupertātemque fatendō effēcēre levem

paupertās, paupertātis f.

noun, third declension

poverty, small means

Slender means rather than want, the opposite of riches (Lewis & Short); real need is egestās.

Other words

  • egestās, egestātis f. — want, destitution

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Verg. G. 1.146: dūrīs urgēns in rēbus egestās, want that presses in hard times

  • inopia, inopiae f. — lack of means, need

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Publ. I 7: Inopiae dēsunt multa, avāritiae omnia, poverty lacks much, greed everything; Traupman 153

  • pauperiēs, pauperiēī f. — poverty

    noun, fifth declension · also used · classical · Hor. C. 1.1.18: indocilis pauperiem patī

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Hor., Verg.; in prose after Augustus)

Examples

  • sed pia Baucis anus parilīque aetāte Philēmōn illā sunt annīs jūnctī juvenālibus, illā cōnsenuēre casā paupertātemque fatendō effēcēre levem nec inīquā mente ferendō

    but good old Baucis and Philemon, of the same age, were married in that cottage in their young years and grew old in it; they made their poverty light by owning it and bearing it without complaintOv. Met. 8.631–634

  • vetus est prōverbium: paupertātem certissimam esse, cum alicujus indigeat, ūtī eō nōn posse, quia ignōrētur, ubi prōjectum jaceat, quod dēsīderātur

    there is an old proverb that the surest poverty is to need something and be unable to use it, because no one knows where the thing you want has been thrownCol. 12.2.3

See also poor, rich, beggar, alms.
